The campaign is very short but still engaging. There’s a great variety of cars and races. The music tracks also sound pretty good. The graphics look amazing, and the optimization is even better - the game runs very smoothly.

The police are absolutely insane here - they’ll do anything to stop you. And once you see “Rhino incoming,” it’s basically RIP for you.

Also liked the small reference to older Need for Speed games at the end - a nice touch for fans. However, the ending felt very unexpected and a bit weird, and it’s a big downside that it just kind of cuts off so abruptly.

Its one of the best NFS games, both story wise and content wise.. Though some people might find a bit short on the option for cars to choose from, the ones in the game are quite intriguing, and keeps you busy all the time upgrading and customizing. It is worth playing still in 2024-25..

I always said that Need for Speed Most Wanted (the old one) was their peak of al NFS games.

There wasn't any other racing game that gave you chills when Styles of Beyond - Nine Thou blasted through your radio while driving a Citroën C1 in real life.

But this game comes close. Like really close.

This game is al fun evading and ramming cops but oh boy! When the heat turns up to 3 you feel like a fresh stuffed turkey on Thankgiving. They just ram all of their shit like you are a bumper car.

The racing is fun and addictive. It's really more an arcade feeling instead of a realistic race simulator like Project Cars. But I like this game more 'cause I want to throttle to max speed and not worry that I'll spin 180 degrees in agony!

Anyways, check it out at a discount!

It's a lot like the old school Most Wanted, however they have managed to take the thrill out of it and replace it with good old grind and a massive price tag. The racing is meh compared to today's options, more akin to the racing games of the PS2 era. The UI is mostly clean but not the best and downright idiotic at times. Like most of the time I can't read any of the race info in daytime. And the post processing they put on it makes it damn hard to even see anything sometimes. The graphics is somehow good and bad at the same time. Like the models are great, but the shaders they use are terrible. To me the cars don't look like they belong in the world. Customization exists... the decal system is great though. The game itself is a lot of grind with little reward. The story makes no sense, but that I can let slide. It is NFS after all. And the music kinda sucks. But those are the bad. The good is that this is a MMO racing game. Fkn sick! Quite fun with friends. And it has this seamless transitions when loading which looks dope. 
6/10. Wouldn't recommend at full price, but if you can get it on sale and like racing games I'm sure you'll enjoy some of this.

I am having fun but there are some glaring issues and general laziness. Biggest issue is a resounding from everyone: cops are ass to deal with unless you cheese them. Yeah not fun when a cop blazes past you when you are already going 200kmph.

Performance shop feels lazy, next to no thought in how things interact with cars. pretty much all the primary parts add the same amount of "power". Then there are the power adders... the thought and game balance to how the turbos and supers was just completely ignored. They should be the bulk of your performance yet the stats do not reflect that in the slightest. You really lose a sense for what realistically makes a car faster. Certain motors which are considered performance holy grails are just a laughing stock. No rhyme or reason to what the engines do.

There is no way to sort cars in the dealership in any way. Makes looking for what you need/want a chore.

Otherwise the customization is great, racing feels pretty nostalgic and object physics are good. I have noticed that a quite a few race routes get recycled but i am not too far to really tell.

PS: EA can eat a gross diseased hog as usual.

You can have a c10 pick up truck out maneuver a Ferrari race car. Driving the cars from the psp version of need for speed and going back to this feels like EA has changed nothing since they started making need for speed.

Palm City is interesting to look at both in the day and night, but isn't really that interesting to race. Like a lot of open world racing games, the races become stale after a while as you're going to be driving over familiar routes with little to no surprises or setpieces added for the sake of the race.

The police chase mechanic starts out interesting enough, but the lack of offensive abilities at higher heat levels means you have to look up areas and guides to exploit the AI by taking jumps, diving in the water, or just getting lucky otherwise your supercar will be caught up to by an SUV and Crown Vic easily, and sent into a barrel roll on the slightest tap of your car. There's no pursuit breakers, hiding spots, they're too resilient to be rammed outright at higher heat levels, and cannot usually be tricked by weaving through traffic or taking sharp corners.

I ended up not finishing due to these two factors, despite liking the customization features and the overall feel of the game despite it being a little simple with its drift mechanics. There's just not enough interesting content here, and what's here is a mixed bag.

Cant say the gameplay itself is bad but it is hit and miss if this game will work or not, plus if it doesnt then its unfixable even if you have a pc that should be more than capable.

I tried to like this game. But I'm shelving this one. I wanted to like this NFS. But the handling is so bad it's just not fun to play for me. I wasn't expecting a sim racer or anything. But it plays like a burnout game without any of the things that I like about Burnout. It doesn't feel like driving at all. It's like a smartphone game almost (You drop the gas and it magically drifts). I wish NFS came back to its black box era. The run, Pro Street, MW had great handling and it was still very arcade-like.

It's the driving. It's not good. Thus, all though presentation-wise looks great. It's not fun for me.

Also: no control mapping?

PD: the Unite mod made the experience WAYY better. But I'll still pass on this game and I don't plan on buying new NFS games for while :'(

Opel reviews: NFS Heat
NFS Heat is probably the best NFS game of the 2010's due to it's exciting mechanics like the day/night cycle that shows the 2 completely different faces of the city or the huge variety of customizable parts. The story (even if it is relatively short) is quite good and the graphics look nice even if games like FH4 are stronger in this category. Finally, I am dissatisfied by the poor variety of cars (where is my Opel Meriva) and I am not a big fan of the arcade-ish driving experience but that SUTUTUTU and the unreal backfire those car spit make up for the drawbacks.
In conclusion, NFS Heat is a game that street racing fans should get even in times when racing games start to feel all the same and honestly pretty boring.

tldr.text: Very Positive (85%): players praise the story and characters most, though those same characters draw the most complaints.
Graphics and mods also win praise, while the price and bugs and crashes are the other common complaints.

details.text: Recent reviews complain much less about the price and the story than reviews overall, so a buyer today is less likely to be put off by either.
Players who have barely played are far less positive than veterans: 37% of their reviews are positive against 93% from those who have logged the most time.
